html:
The global security landscape is dominated by an escalating confrontation between the US and Iran, as a 60-day ceasefire expired with no diplomatic or military off-ramp in sight. Trump today threatened "tremendous economic consequences" on any country aiding Iran and announced the initiation of the "most crushing economic operation" against Tehran, warning of "unprecedented economic warfare."

US-Iran Tensions: The significant US economic pressure follows reports that Iran is considering attacking US military targets in Europe if Trump escalates the conflict, with potential targets including a base in Bulgaria and undersea fiber optic cables. Iran negotiator Ghalibaf stated the Strait of Hormuz will not open until US demands are met, while a Leader’s adviser asserted Iranian control over the waterway. The UAE has already responded to the heightened tensions by accusing Tehran of firing ballistic missiles at shipping and halting all trade and financial transactions with Iran until further notice. This situation has reportedly alarmed South Korea, shaking a 72-year alliance due to a dispute with the US over Iran and the scaling back of military drills. The US military, facing long-range missile shortages and prolonged deployments in the conflict, has pivoted its geopolitical attention away from Asia, while secretly establishing a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.

Middle East Security: Amidst the wider regional tensions, Israel has opened bids for a "highly-sensitive West Bank settlement project," drawing condemnation from the UK's foreign secretary who called it "an unacceptable and destructive act." This comes as Israeli airstrikes continue in Gaza, reportedly killing police chiefs and multiple Palestinians, with Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad accusing Israel of undermining stalled peace plans. International outrage has also mounted after Israel decided not to prosecute over the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, prompting Australia's foreign minister to summon the Israeli ambassador, while Israel did admit its soldiers fired at the car in which Hind Rajab was killed and opened a criminal investigation. Trump's son-in-law Kushner met Hamas regarding Trump's Gaza plan, with critics saying Israel is "wreaking havoc in Gaza." The US is also set to provide $206 million for a Gaza peacekeeping force.

Ukraine Developments: In Eastern Europe, Ukraine faces internal political instability as Zelenskyy fired a top aide amid a graft probe, with Ukraine's ex-defense minister demanding elections. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian diver has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline bombings, with German prosecutors confirming the arrest of a second suspect. The conflict continues with reports of a warehouse burning near Moscow and Ukrainian drone crews preparing to strike again, while Russia and Ukraine exchanged 206 prisoners with UAE mediation.

US Domestic and Economy: The US national debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time, while Trump led the press corps on a tour of White House renovations. Despite these domestic concerns and the ongoing Iran war, Trump is also planning to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un later this year to revive their first-term relationship. On trade, the US delayed a 50% tariff on Canadian imports as Prime Minister Carney hailed "significant progress" in finalizing a new deal ahead of a weekend tariff deadline. Separately, Donald Trump's secretary of state, Marco Rubio, announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, which the ICC called a "flagrant attack" on its independence.

Global Events: Globally, a severe Ebola outbreak in Congo has reached 5,000 cases, killing 2,378 people and outpacing response efforts. In Central African Republic, a gold mine collapse killed more than 100 people. Indonesia saw an 84-year-old woman rescued three days after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake killed at least 73 people and displaced nearly 60,000. Australia and New Zealand dispatched over 240 firefighters to aid in battling destructive US wildfires. Additionally, Prince Harry and Meghan are reportedly moving back to Britain this month, six years after leaving for the US.
